Spain exempts self-custody wallets from crypto tax reporting

Spain's tax authorities have confirmed that cryptocurrency held in self-custody wallets — where the owner controls the private keys — does not need to be reported under Form 721, the country's disclosure form for foreign-held digital assets. The exemption hinges on one condition: no third party holds the assets on your behalf.

The rule draws a clean line between personal custody and exchange or custodial holdings abroad, which remain reportable. Simple in principle, potentially significant in practice — Spain just gave self-custody a regulatory edge.

Geography Returns With a Knife

The global economy spent three decades pretending distance was dead. Then Iran squeezed the Strait of Hormuz and reminded everybody that oil still needs a narrow piece of water, a ship and a captain willing to enter a kill zone.

The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has turned Hormuz into a tariff booth operated with mines, drones and missiles. 

Oil has begun moving again, but largely under U.S. Navy escort. 

Iran’s power is not technological parity with Washington. It is the map: one shoreline beside the world’s most important energy chokepoint. 

That is why a regional war now reaches supermarkets, diesel pumps, factories and farms far from the Gulf. Higher energy prices feed inflation. 

Inflation pressures central banks. Interest rates rise. Transport costs jump. The same route that carries Gulf oil also carries the cost of fertilizer, food and electricity to countries with no vote in the war.

The Houthis learned the same lesson at Bab el-Mandeb, the southern gateway to the Red Sea. Iran cannot match the American fleet. The Houthis cannot match Iran. 

But each can sit beside a corridor that richer countries built their economies around and charge the planet for passing through.

Globalization did not abolish geography. It put supply chains on top of it and called the result resilience.

The new world order is brutally physical. Ukraine is a hinge between Europe and Eurasia. Taiwan anchors the island chain off China’s coast. 

The Panama Canal needs rain. The Rhine needs water. Hormuz needs an agreement, or an escort fleet. Every app still depends on a port, a river, a cable, a refinery and a strait somebody else can close.

Trump said at the UN, “To the victor belong the spoils,” speaking about Venezuela’s oil. Iran heard the same doctrine and found its own spoils: tolls on global trade. The American answer is naval power. The Iranian answer is geography.

The ships move again only when a warship says they can. That is not free trade. It is a convoy system with a Bloomberg terminal.
